title: Migration-0018 oversized-stack reviews with quantity <=100 are permanently unresolvable
description:
Post-merge review of PR #455 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

A migrated `oversized-stack` adoption review whose row quantity is ≤ 100 is permanently unresolvable: the quarantine (which blocks item usage, resets, context projection, custody, and attunement) can never be lifted by any accepted resolution.

Code facts (all verified):

- Migration `packages/core/data/migrations/0018_inventory_adoption_review.sql` classifies migrated markers as `review_kind='oversized-stack'` purely by matching the legacy reason string (`LIKE 'stateful legacy stack quantity % exceeds the reviewed adoption maximum of % singleton instances'`). It never checks the row's *current* `inventory.quantity`.
- The kind→action mapping is exclusive: `oversized-stack` accepts only `set-reviewed-quantity` (`itemAdoptionReview.ts:48-49`, and the SQL CHECK on `inventory_adoption_resolution` enforces the same pairing at the schema level).
- The resolver rejects `set-reviewed-quantity` when `row.quantity <= MAX_MAGIC_ITEM_ADOPTION_SINGLETONS` (=100): `itemAdoption.ts:347-349` — "set-reviewed-quantity applies only to a quarantined stack above 100".

So any pre-migration marker carrying that reason string on a row whose quantity is now ≤ 100 (the legacy markers were model-writable advisory JSON, so the reason and the actual quantity were never atomically coupled; quantity could also have been legitimately corrected after the marker was written) becomes a permanent quarantine with no GM escape hatch.

## Fix direction (per review recommendation)

Migration checksums are immutable — do not edit 0018. Instead either:

1. New migration that reclassifies `oversized-stack` reviews whose row quantity is ≤ 100 as `malformed-evidence` (whose `discard-evidence` resolution works and preserves the raw evidence in `discarded_structure_json`); or
2. A resolver compatibility rule permitting an evidence-backed no-reduction resolution for this case — but note the `inventory_adoption_resolution` CHECK constrains kind→action pairs at the schema level, so option 1 (reclassification) is the cleaner path; option 2 would itself need a migration to widen the CHECK.

Add a regression test constructing the impossible state (oversized-stack review + quantity ≤ 100) and asserting it is resolvable after the fix.

Related: sold-item `returned` payment bypass and the numeric-conservation dice-modifier gate, filed from the same review.
